psychoanalysis->family-systems:reacts.note: Family therapists were dissatisfied with looking for causes only inside the individual mind.

cbt->trauma:develops.note: Exposure and cognitive restructuring became the basis of trauma-focused treatment.

mbsr-program->mbct-model:develops.note: Adapts the MBSR course into a version for preventing depressive relapse.

common-factors->ebp:bridges.note: Common-factors research means that 'evidence' must include the relationship and patient characteristics.

attachment->eft:bridges.note: Johnson applied attachment theory to couple therapy.

diathesis-stress->dimensional:bridges.note: The diathesis-stress idea extends into cross-diagnostic dimensional research.

transactional-stress-model->app-health-p.note: The appraisal and coping model is used for chronic illness and stress management.

biopsychosocial->app-health-psychology:a.note: Health psychology uses this framework to integrate biological and psychosocial factors.

mbsr->app-health-psychology:applies.note: Mindfulness courses are used in pain, stress and chronic illness care.

forgetting-curve->app-education-learning.note: The basis for spaced review and retrieval practice.

how-people-learn->app-education-learning.note: Turns cognitive and developmental research into teaching principles.

sociocultural->app-education-learning:ap.note: The zone of proximal development and scaffolding become the basis of instructional design.

aba->app-education-learning:applies.note: Uses behavior analysis to improve special education and classroom behavior.

field-theory->app-industrial-organizatio.note: Group dynamics and action research became the starting point of organizational development.

expectancy-theory->app-industrial-organi.note: Used to explain work motivation and performance management.

big-five->app-industrial-organizational:.note: Personality assessment is used for selection and development.

intelligence-testing->app-industrial-org.note: Ability tests are used for selection, though with ongoing fairness disputes.

misinformation-effect->app-forensic:appl.note: Changed practice on eyewitness testimony and questioning methods.

affordances->app-human-factors:applies.note: 'Affordance' became a core concept in product and interface design.

working-memory-model->app-human-factors:.note: The limits of working memory shape the design of interfaces and workflows.

prospect-theory->app-public-policy:appli.note: Loss aversion and reference points shape the design of defaults and incentives.

cbt->app-self-help:applies.note: CBT methods were written into self-help books and exercises, some supported by controlled trials.

habit-loop->app-self-help:applies.note: The cue-routine-reward loop is used to design personal habit change.

experimental->behaviorism:reacts.note: Opposed introspection and argued for studying only observable behavior.

functionalism->behaviorism:develops.note: The focus on adaptation and function paved the way for the objective study of behavior.

behaviorism->cognitive-revolution:reacts.note: Language and thought cannot be explained by stimulus and response alone.

neo-behaviorism->cognitive-revolution:br.note: Tolman's cognitive maps brought internal representations inside behaviorism.

gestalt->field-theory:develops.note: Lewin, trained in the Berlin Gestalt school, applied the 'field' idea to social behavior.

gestalt->cognitive-psychology:bridges.note: Research on holistic perception and problem solving was absorbed into cognitive psychology.

cognitive-development->cognitive-revolut.note: Piaget's study of mental structures is one European source of the cognitive turn.

social-learning->cognitive-psychology:br.note: Observational learning brings attention and memory into learning theory.

psychoanalysis->cognitive-therapies:reac.note: Ellis and Beck were trained in psychoanalysis but set out separately, finding it hard to test.

cognitive-revolution->cognitive-therapie.note: Provided the theoretical language that beliefs and information processing shape emotion.

behavior-therapy->cbt:merges.note: Techniques such as exposure and behavioral activation are folded into the integrated model.

cognitive-therapies->cbt:merges.note: Cognitive reappraisal is folded into the integrated model.

dissociation->psychoanalysis:develops.note: Freud studied with Charcot in 1885, beginning from research on hypnosis and hysteria.

dissociation->trauma:bridges.note: Janet's dissociation theory was rediscovered in trauma research in the 1980s.

psychoanalysis->person-centered:reacts.note: Rejects the view that people are driven by drives and believes in an inherent tendency to grow.

behaviorism->needs:reacts.note: Humanistic psychology called itself the 'third force' and opposed behaviorism's mechanistic view.

analytical-psychology->needs:bridges.note: The ideas of individuation and self-actualization are related, though with no direct teacher-student line.

object-relations->attachment:merges.note: Bowlby's training in object relations brought in the idea of internal working models.

ethology->attachment:merges.note: Animal studies of imprinting and parent-offspring bonds gave attachment an evolutionary perspective.

attachment->mentalization:develops.note: Uses attachment research to explain how the ability to understand others' minds forms.

psychoanalysis->psychosocial:develops.note: Erikson expanded psychosexual stages into lifelong psychosocial stages.

sociocultural->cultural:bridges.note: The source of the idea that mental processes are mediated by cultural tools.

individual-differences->behavior-genetic.note: Galton's twin and family studies were its methodological precursors.

individual-differences->intelligence-tes.note: Galton's measurement and statistical tradition continues in intelligence testing.

g-factor->big-five:develops.note: Applies factor analysis methods to personality dimensions.

person-situation->trait:critiques.note: Cross-situational consistency of behavior is lower than trait theory assumes.

cognitive-revolution->cognitive-neurosci.note: Provides cognitive models that can be tested in the brain.

neuropsychology->cognitive-neuroscience:.note: Provides the methods of brain-injury cases and imaging.

hebbian->connectionism:develops.note: 'Neurons that fire together wire together' became the learning rule of networks.

stress-physiology->biopsychosocial:bridg.note: Stress links social circumstances to physical disease.

nosology->dsm:develops.note: Kraepelin's descriptive classification tradition was systematized in the DSM.

psychopharmacology->dsm:bridges.note: Drug trials need reliable diagnostic criteria, which drove DSM-III.

dimensional->dsm:critiques.note: Categorical diagnosis brings problems of comorbidity and heterogeneity.

cognitive-neuroscience->dimensional:merg.note: RDoC organizes research by neural circuits, drawing on cognitive neuroscience.

big-five->dimensional:bridges.note: HiTOP borrows the dimensional and hierarchical structure of personality.

mbsr->third-wave:merges.note: Mindfulness practice became a component of several third-wave therapies.

cbt->third-wave:develops.note: Shifts from changing the content of thoughts to changing one's relationship with thoughts.

morita->third-wave:bridges.note: 'Go with the flow, do what needs doing' is close to acceptance-based approaches, though with no direct lineage.

learned-helplessness->positive:develops.note: Seligman moved from studying helplessness to studying optimism and well-being.

needs->positive:develops.note: Inherits the focus on growth and potential.

positive->needs:critiques.note: Criticizes humanistic psychology for lacking empirical method and calls for measurement and experiment.

heuristics-biases->app-public-policy:app.note: Behavioral economics and 'nudging' are built on this foundation.

cultural->cognitive-psychology:critiques.note: Many 'universal' cognitive conclusions hold only in Western samples.

open-science->social-cognition:critiques.note: Several social priming effects have failed to replicate.

affective-neuroscience->trauma:bridges.note: Research on fear and threat circuits provides mechanisms for trauma responses.

psychoanalysis->behavior-therapy:reacts.note: Eysenck and Wolpe criticized psychoanalysis for lacking evidence of efficacy and advocated treatment based on learning principles.

person-centered->common-factors:develops.note: Rogers's empathy, genuineness and acceptance became a major source of common-factors research.

gestalt->gestalt-therapy:bridges.note: The Perls drew on ideas of wholeness and figure-ground, but this is not an extension of Gestalt psychology.

evolutionary->attachment:bridges.note: Explains attachment as an adaptation with survival value, a view that comes from evolutionary thinking.

connectionism->deep-learning-models:deve.note: Multilayer networks plus big data and computing power.

deep-learning-models->llm-cognition:deve.note: The same class of networks is used to process language.

operant->reward-prediction:bridges.note: Reinforcement is written as a computable prediction-error signal.

reward-prediction->computational-rl:deve.note: The same algorithms drive artificial agents.

behavior-genetics->psychiatric-genomics:.note: Moves from estimating heritability with twins to finding loci in the genome.

cognitive-neuroscience->connectome:devel.note: Moves from single brain areas to whole-brain connectivity.

cognitive-neuroscience->abcd:develops.note: Puts brain imaging into large-scale longitudinal research.

big-five->digital-footprints:develops.note: Uses online behavioral data to predict Big Five scores.

network-psychometrics->dsm:critiques.note: Symptoms trigger one another, so there is no need to assume a single underlying disease.

open-science->large-replications:develop.note: Turns 'can it be replicated?' into a question that can be answered statistically.

cultural->weird:develops.note: Advances findings on cultural differences into a critique of sampling.

moral-development->moral-foundations:rea.note: Holds that moral judgment starts from intuition and that reasoning comes later.

social-cognition->misinformation:develop.note: Applies research on belief formation to the online information environment.

pp2->positive:critiques.note: Focuses only on the positive, ignoring the place of suffering in a good life.

mbsr->self-compassion:bridges.note: Draws on Buddhist compassion and includes mindfulness as a component.

cognitive-neuroscience->neuropsychoanaly.note: Tests psychoanalytic concepts with brain-injury and imaging research.

psychoanalysis->psychodynamic-evidence:d.note: Tests dynamic therapy with randomized controlled trials and meta-analyses.

cbt->unified-protocol:develops.note: One protocol addresses the shared mechanisms of several emotional disorders.

third-wave->process-based:develops.note: Moves from 'which therapy' to 'which process of change.'

cbt->digital-mental-health:develops.note: Turns structured treatment into programs and apps.

psychopharmacology->psychedelic-therapy:.note: Drugs and psychotherapy are combined in one treatment course.

trauma->icd-11:develops.note: The consequences of long-term repeated trauma are listed separately as complex PTSD.

psychological-types->factor-personality:.note: Eysenck turned the terms introversion and extraversion into measurable dimensions.

psychological-types->mbti:develops.note: Myers and her mother used this to build a forced-choice type questionnaire.

life-stages->lifespan:bridges.note: Jung's account of midlife transition is one of the early sources of adult development research.

active-imagination->sandplay:develops.note: Kalff developed sandplay on Jung's advice and treated it as a form of active imagination.

analytical-psychology->app-self-help:app.note: Jung's advice to Hazzard, relayed by Wilson, became one of the sources of the self-help fellowship.
